PAPERS.title: Single-scattering look-up table for remote sensing and in situ black carbon studies
PAPERS.pm: Black carbon fractal aggregates, single-scattering properties 0.35-2.3 um
PAPERS.n: Tabulates single-scattering properties of fractal-like soot aggregates (refractive index 1.95-0.96i; fractal dimension 1.4-2.8; 1-4,096 monomers of 15-25 nm radius) across 0.35-2.3 um for PACE retrievals, giving a speed-up of at least 10^6 over direct computation. As a test it reproduces the low single-scattering albedo of in situ ACTIVATE aircraft aerosol. Limitation: bare, identical, touching monomers only - no coating, no polydispersity, no necking - so aged, internally mixed BC (the ambient case) and its absorption enhancement fall outside the table; agreement with one campaign is a plausibility check, not validation. Relevance: moderate - fast BC optics is what multi-wavelength absorption channels on low-cost nodes need to convert attenuation to mass with a defensible morphology assumption.

PAPERS.title: Columnar optical properties of locally emitted light-absorbing carbonaceous aerosols
PAPERS.pm: BC and BrC absorption (AE33, 370/470 nm), AOD/AAOD/SSA at 550 nm
PAPERS.n: Paired surface and mountain-station aethalometer (AE33) measurements in Beijing under pollution controls; an ensemble HYSPLIT + concentration-weighted-trajectory screen isolates locally emitted events, and a wavelength-dependent AAE method derives BrC absorption at 370 and 470 nm. BrC falls off more steeply with height than BC, so the BC share of absorption rises aloft. During local events, noon AOD and AAOD rise 1.91- and 1.93-fold and SSA shows a noon minimum. Limitation: columnar optics are reconstructed from two point sites plus Mie theory for scattering, not measured by a sun photometer or lidar, and trajectory screening of 'local' is model-dependent. Relevance: moderate - surface BrC/BC ratios from ground nodes do not transfer to the column that satellite fusion uses.

PAPERS.title: An NB-IoT-Based Architecture with Spatial-Statistical Analytics for Cross-Domain Air and Water Quality Monitoring in Aquaculture
PAPERS.pm: Low-cost PM1/PM2.5/PM10 channel among multi-pollutant air nodes
PAPERS.n: Edge nodes with low-cost air (PM1/2.5/10, O3, TVOC, eCO2, T/RH, UV) and water sensors stream over NB-IoT and MQTT to a cloud database with IDW mapping and alerting. A deployment at one aquaculture facility logged 14,400 one-minute records with 99.24% raw packet delivery; analyses correct for autocorrelation (N_eff ~892) and FDR, and the headline findings are air-temperature/dissolved-oxygen and humidity/turbidity correlations. Limitation for this watch: no PM sensor is co-located with a reference, calibrated or humidity-corrected, so the PM channel is uncharacterised; the PM data enter none of the reported results. Relevance: low - the telemetry (gateway-free NB-IoT, packet delivery) is the transferable part; it says nothing about PM data quality.

PAPERS.title: Aggregated non-methane organic and inorganic gases as indicators of aged particulate matter induced by traffic
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - aggregate NMVOC as proxy for aged traffic PM (by deposit teaser)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: RSC deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. The deposit carries a one-line teaser: aggregate NMVOC emissions were found to indicate the organic fraction of the subsequently aged PM. If it holds, a gas-phase total (cheap to sense) could flag secondary organic PM that optical counters see only after ageing; the data and the lag structure are unknown. Nothing about data, method, sample size or estimates can be stated from the deposit, and this watch does not infer a method from a title. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Evaluating Graph-Centrality Context for Station-Level Correction of CAMS Air Quality Reanalysis in Lombardy from 2018 to 2021
PAPERS.pm: CAMS reanalysis PM2.5, PM10, NOx, NO2 corrected to ARPA stations
PAPERS.n: Corrects CAMS European reanalysis to ARPA Lombardia station observations (2018-2021) by treating stations as nodes of a multiplex graph and feeding six centrality measures (including an OpenStreetMap-context adapted PageRank) into GTWR, XGBoost and random forest with spatio-temporal kriging, under station, temporal and combined holdout. Station-holdout XGBoost reaches R2 up to 0.66 for NO2; OSM-context centrality helps NOx and PM2.5, is mixed for NO2, and helps PM10 only temporally with RF-STK. Limitation: the abstract gives no PM2.5 R2 or RMSE, gains are described qualitatively, and centrality is computed on the regulatory station layout itself, so transfer to a denser or differently sited network is untested. Relevance: moderate - graph features of node placement are directly computable for low-cost networks.

PAPERS.title: Persistent cold air pools and associated sustained haze pollution in Taiyuan Basin
PAPERS.pm: Surface PM2.5 vs basin meteorology (soundings, valley heat deficit, WRF)
PAPERS.n: Builds a refined detector for persistent cold-air pools from multi-station and sounding data in the Taiyuan Basin (2018-2022), validates WRF for PCAP meteorology, and identifies 56 events, mostly September-March, winter ones commonly lasting >48 h. Events carry stronger surface inversions, larger valley heat deficit and suppressed ventilation; PM2.5 peaks lag heat-deficit intensification by 12 h (R = 0.55). Warm advection aloft maintains PCAPs and lee-side subsidence warming reinforces them; strong cold advection ends them. Limitation: R = 0.55 on a single basin, with emissions held implicit, so the 12-h lag is descriptive. Relevance: moderate - a 12-h lead from a sounding-derived metric is a usable forecasting feature, and basin networks must site nodes at more than one elevation to see the pool.

PAPERS.title: Organosulfate-driven amplification of secondary organic aerosol formation from isoprene oxidation intermediates: Coupled effects of SO2 and relative humidity
PAPERS.pm: SOA from methacrolein/OH photooxidation; organosulfates (GC-MS, ATR-FTIR)
PAPERS.n: Smog-chamber methacrolein/OH photooxidation at high (61-65%), medium (20-22%) and low (9-12%) RH with varied SO2. Particle mass, peak number, geometric mean diameter and SOA yield all rise with initial SO2 at every RH; with SO2 present, SOA mass rises as RH falls, attributed to lower wall loss of hydrophilic species and less dilution of aerosol acidity. ATR-FTIR shows organosulfates and inorganic sulfate in the particle phase. Limitation: chamber concentrations and wall-loss corrections dominate yield estimates, and no yields are reported in the abstract; transfer to ambient isoprene-SO2 mixing is assumed. Relevance: low-moderate - acid-catalysed SOA is part of why the optical-to-mass ratio of low-cost sensors drifts with season and RH.

PAPERS.title: What drives long-term variations in biomass burning emissions in China?
PAPERS.pm: Biomass-burning PM2.5, PM10, EC, OC and gas emissions, 2008-2023
PAPERS.n: A 2008-2023 inventory of domestic and open biomass burning with Kaya/LMDI decomposition of PM2.5 emission change. 2008 emissions were 3.22 Mt PM2.5, 0.50 Mt EC and 1.41 Mt OC; all species fell 50-65% by 2023. Domestic burning declined mainly through the economic factor on burned biomass (183.4% of the change) and urbanisation (54.7%); open straw burning fell through activity intensity (-115%), whose effect weakened after 2017. Limitation: LMDI partitions an identity, it does not test causation, and activity data for domestic and open burning are the weakest inputs of any Chinese inventory; no uncertainty bounds are given. Relevance: low-moderate - the declining rural smoke signal is a baseline shift any rural sensor trend analysis has to account for.

PAPERS.title: Comparative analysis of multiple health risks from different air pollution events
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved number 3 nm-10 um, PM2.5 composition, OP; lung deposition model
PAPERS.n: Online and offline measurements in Beijing (Feb-May 2019) classify haze (83% secondary), firework (31% firework) and dust (50% dust) events and compare risk metrics against clean days. Haze and firework particles deposit mainly tracheobronchially and pulmonary, dust in extrathoracic and TB regions; ultrafines are >=81% of deposited number in every event. Carcinogenic risk exceeds 1e-4 in all events (7.6, 4.2 and 1.5 times clean-day 2.3e-4); hazard index reaches 241, 100 and 37 (firework, dust, haze) vs 23 clean. PM2.5 OP is 0.74-0.82 vs 0.47 nmol/min/m3 clean. Limitation: one spring, one site, few events per type; HI and TCR are deterministic screening indices with default toxicity values, not health outcomes. Relevance: moderate - event rankings flip by metric, which a mass-only network cannot reproduce.

PAPERS.title: Seasonal and Pollution-Level Variations in PM2.5-Bound PFASs and Associated Health Risks in Jinan, a Typical Northern Chinese Industrial City
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5-bound PFASs (17 compounds, LC-MS/MS), 163 filters
PAPERS.n: 163 PM2.5 filters over a year (Dec 2023-Nov 2024) in Jinan, 17 PFASs by LC-MS/MS. Total PFAS ranks winter 133.8 > autumn 123.6 ~ summer 123.5 > spring 97.1 pg/m3; in summer and autumn concentrations were numerically higher on clean than on slightly polluted days. No monotonic relation of total PFAS with single meteorological variables; compound responses depend on chain length. PFOA and short-chain PFCAs make up 73.1% of estimated intake and PFOA 95.6% of risk. Limitation: 'numerically higher' differences are not tested, one site, and risk uses reference doses for ingestion-derived toxicity. Relevance: moderate - a PM2.5 hazard that is decoupled from PM2.5 mass is invisible to any mass sensor, whatever its calibration.

PAPERS.title: Metropolitan atmospheric microplastics: Characteristics and its inputs to fluvial system
PAPERS.pm: Atmospheric microplastic deposition (n/m2/day), fibres and fragments
PAPERS.n: Deposition sampling across urban, suburban and exurban Chengdu: 246, 192 and 177 items/m2/day respectively, dominated by fibres and fragments. PCA finds three source patterns (73.9% of variance), the largest a mixed daily-plastic-products source (55.1%). Abundance tracks precipitation intensity, weakly wind direction, not temperature or RH, and shows no relation to other air pollutants. Rainy-season input to the river system is estimated at 689-1,088 kg. Limitation: deposition flux, not airborne concentration or inhalable size fraction, so there is no exposure metric; identification method and lower size cut are not given in the abstract. Relevance: low - the absent correlation with regulated pollutants means PM networks are no proxy for airborne plastics.

PAPERS.title: Suspended Atmospheric Microplastics in the Outskirts of Seoul City: Seasonal Variability, Correlation with Meteorology
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - suspended airborne microplastics (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. PAPERS.title: Estimating Speciated Input Concentrations for Biomass Burning Organic Aerosol Modeling
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - speciated BB VOC/POA model inputs (by deposit teaser)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: RSC deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. PAPERS.title: Primary nitrated phenol emissions from heavy-duty diesel vehicles based on real-world activity data in Hunan, China
PAPERS.pm: Nitrated phenols (light-absorbing BrC), filter + PUF exhaust sampling
PAPERS.n: Combines tandem filter/PUF exhaust emission factors with real-world heavy-duty diesel activity data to inventory primary nitrated phenols in Hunan for 2025: 1,196.8 kg/yr, 48.3% from container trucks, 22.9% freight trucks, 17.7% buses; China IV and V vehicles 84.1%. 4-Nitrophenol dominates (334.9 kg/yr). Monthly totals range 76.8 kg (Feb) to 114.4 kg (Dec), and five cities emit 53.9%. Limitation: emission factors from a limited test fleet are scaled to a province, the particle/gas split is not reported in the abstract, and no uncertainty is given. Relevance: low - nitrated phenols are a light-absorbing BrC component near freight corridors, relevant to multi-wavelength absorption channels, but the mass involved is trivial against PM2.5.

PAPERS.title: Delayed Coal Plant Retirements in the Era of Data Centers Carry a Measurable Mortality Cost
PAPERS.pm: Coal-plant-attributable PM2.5, plant-specific source-receptor modelling
PAPERS.n: Of 50 US coal plants scheduled (Jan 2024) to retire before 2035, 20 had later or removed dates by Jan 2026. Projecting plant-attributable PM2.5 and mortality among Medicare beneficiaries for 2026-2035, the revised schedule adds 1,256 deaths (1,136-1,376), 3.1 times the burden of the original schedule. Eighteen of the 20 plants sit in balancing authorities with hyperscale data-centre demand, and several federal orders and utility filings cite data-centre growth. Limitation: the interval reflects concentration-response uncertainty only, not dispersion-model or future-emission uncertainty; operating hours of delayed plants are assumed; attribution to data centres is circumstantial, not causal; preprint. Relevance: moderate - coal-sulfate PM2.5 is regional and secondary, so it is a background term networks see as a baseline, not as a local plume.

PAPERS.title: Assessment of the significance of urban vegetation in air phytoremediation: Quantitative analysis of particulate matter removal
PAPERS.pm: Leaf-deposited PM in 0.2-2.5, 2.5-11 and 11-100 um fractions; elemental composition
PAPERS.n: Leaves of five morphologies were sampled every fourth day for a year, leaf-surface PM quantified in three size classes and scaled to 20 dominant species and canopy cover. Delhi's urban forest (23% of area) removed 527 +/- 301 t PM2.5 and 7,907 +/- 1,079 t total PM - about 1.08% of annual PM2.5 emissions in the 2018 SAFAR inventory. Directly measured removal is ~24% of the deposition-velocity estimate for PM2.5 and ~4.6% for PM10; leaf loading saturates in Nov-Jan. Fine deposits are enriched in Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn and Pb. Limitation: five morphologies extrapolated to 20 species, wash-off and resuspension partly estimated, an emissions denominator from 2018; preprint. Relevance: moderate - urban greening claims based on deposition-velocity models overstate removal four-fold.

PAPERS.title: Associations of Outdoor Air Pollution With Cause-specific Mortality in Metastatic Prostate Cancer: A cohort study
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 and NO2 at diagnosis, 1-km exposure models
PAPERS.n: 33,384 men with metastatic prostate cancer (11 US registries, diagnosed 2000-2015, followed to 2018); 1-km PM2.5 and NO2 at the diagnosis address; Cox and IPW cause-specific models. Per IQR PM2.5, cardiovascular mortality HR 1.04 (1.02-1.07), with 4th/5th vs 1st quintile HR 1.18 and 1.21; ADT-treated men with high vs low PM2.5 had HR 1.19 (1.05-1.34), interaction p = 0.051. NO2 was associated only with prostate-cancer death in the top quintile (HR 1.07, 1.01-1.13). Limitation: one address at diagnosis, no smoking or cardiovascular history in registry data, and cause-of-death coding in metastatic cancer is unreliable; the IQR is not stated in the abstract; preprint. Relevance: low-moderate - a high-risk population whose acute exposures personal sensors could resolve.

PAPERS.title: Air pollution and criminal behavior: a nationwide case-crossover analysis in China
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, SO2, O3 (six pollutants, WQS mixture)
PAPERS.n: Time-stratified case-crossover of 483,718 crime events in China (2013-2019) with conditional logistic regression per pollutant and weighted-quantile-sum for the mixture. Per IQR on the event day, crime rose 1.66% for PM2.5, 1.88% PM10, 4.03% NO2, 2.03% CO, 2.81% SO2 and 1.30% O3; WQS index +3.22% per unit. Associations were stronger in the cold season, the north and lower-SES regions, and for violent crime and theft. Limitation: every pollutant is 'positive', which is what shared confounding by weather, daylight and outdoor activity patterns looks like; exposure is assigned at a coarse scale to events of unknown offender residence; no CIs in the abstract. Relevance: low - a behavioural endpoint with acute timing, where personal or hyperlocal exposure would separate PM from co-pollutants.

PAPERS.title: Daily Exceedance of World Health Organization Air Pollutant Guidelines and Cognitive Aging
PAPERS.pm: Annual count of days above WHO daily guideline for PM2.5, PM10, NO2
PAPERS.n: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, 12,235 adults 50+ (waves 1-10, 2002-2023). Exposure is the number of days above WHO daily guideline values in the year before baseline, modelled at the residence, adjusted for the annual mean. NO2 exceedance days (75th percentile vs median) predicted faster 14-year decline: memory -0.09 SD (-0.17 to -0.01), fluency -0.10 SD (-0.19 to 0.00). PM2.5 and PM10 exceedance days were not associated with decline or baseline cognition. Limitation: exceedance count and annual mean are highly collinear, so the 'peak beyond mean' effect is fragile; one exposure year; attrition in ageing cohorts is cognition-dependent; preprint. Relevance: moderate - a null for PM peak frequency is exactly what high-time-resolution networks are positioned to retest.

PAPERS.title: Role of Neighborhood Vulnerability and Opportunity in the Association Between Prenatal Air Pollution and Autism-Related Traits
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal PM2.5, NO2, O3 at residence (pregnancy and trimester means)
PAPERS.n: 8,598 mother-child pairs from 35 ECHO sites; pregnancy and trimester PM2.5, NO2 and O3 at residence; Social Responsiveness Scale analysed by GEE, stratified by census-tract SVI and Child Opportunity Index quintiles, with interaction p < 0.10 as 'suggestive'. O3 interacted with SVI (p = 0.07) and COI (p = 0.01): beta 0.05 (-0.005 to 0.10) in lowest SVI and 0.04 (0.00 to 0.08) in highest COI. Trimester PM2.5 also showed interactions, but no stratum estimate was significant. Limitation: a liberal interaction threshold across many strata and trimesters invites false positives, and the O3 signal appears in the advantaged strata, contrary to the hypothesis. Relevance: low - the PM2.5 finding is null within strata.

PAPERS.title: Developmental PM2.5 exposure and stage-dependent kidney senescence
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - developmental PM2.5 exposure (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: PubMed (Korean Society of Nephrology) deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. The title describes kidney senescence after developmental PM2.5 exposure by life stage. Neither the species nor the exposure route is recoverable. Nothing about data, method, sample size or estimates can be stated from the deposit, and this watch does not infer a method from a title. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Bulk PM2.5 Masks Oxidative Potential and Reactive Oxygen Species Responses by Metal-Organic Complexation in PM1 and PM1-2.5 Mixtures
PAPERS.pm: Roadside PM1 and PM1-2.5 extracts; OP (AA, DTT), cellular ROS, mitochondrial superoxide
PAPERS.n: Roadside PM1 and PM1-2.5 were tested separately and mixed. Mixing is antagonistic on every endpoint - interaction factor 0.65-0.81 for ascorbate OP, 0.80-0.93 for DTT OP, 0.10-0.88 for cellular ROS and 0.43-0.78 for mitochondrial superoxide - whereas metal-free biomass-burning PM is strictly additive. Cu2+-humic acid mixtures reproduce the antagonism (IF 0.22-0.95), and EPR shows complexed Cu forming nonlinearly with the HA:Cu ratio, explaining why studies disagree. Limitation: one roadside site, extract-based assays, and Cu-HA as the single model complex; whether in vivo lining fluid reproduces the complexation is untested. Relevance: high - bulk-PM2.5 OP, the metric proposed as a toxicity-weighted complement to mass, understates the oxidative burden of its size fractions; size-resolved sampling is needed to interpret it.

PAPERS.title: ANKRD22 contributes to NF-kB-associated inflammatory responses in alveolar type II epithelial cells during PM2.5-triggered airway inflammation
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 instillation (mouse) and A549 exposure; dose not in abstract
PAPERS.n: PM2.5 raised ANKRD22 in alveolar type II cells in a mouse airway-inflammation model and in A549 cells. AT-II-specific ANKRD22 knockout mice had less BALF leukocytosis and neutrophilia, histological inflammation and IL-6/CXCL1; siRNA knockdown in A549 lowered IL6, IL8, IL1B, CXCL1 and CXCL2. PM2.5 increased p50, phospho-IKKb, IkBa and RELA, and the non-canonical p52/RELB arm, all attenuated by ANKRD22 loss. Limitation: particle source, dose and dosimetry are not given in the abstract, A549 is a poor AT-II surrogate, and the knockout readouts are acute. Relevance: low - mechanism only; no exposure metric that a monitoring network could map onto.

PAPERS.title: Acorus gramineus Solander Preserves Corneal Epithelial Barrier Integrity against PM2.5-Induced EMT-Like Remodeling
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 on human corneal epithelial spheroids; dose not in abstract
PAPERS.n: Human corneal epithelial cells grown as 3D spheroids were exposed to PM2.5 with or without an Acorus gramineus root extract. PM2.5 destabilised spheroids without marked cytotoxicity, lowered transepithelial resistance, disrupted ZO-1, ZO-3 and occludin, induced EMT-like markers (N-cadherin, vimentin, MMPs) and cytokines, with TGF-b/Smad activation; the extract reversed these. Limitation: particle source and concentration are not stated in the abstract, no in vivo or tear-film model, and the therapeutic arm is a crude herbal extract. Relevance: low - the ocular surface is an underexamined direct-contact target, but nothing here quantifies dose.

PAPERS.title: Gene-environment interaction in neurodevelopment: Setd5 haploinsufficiency and prenatal carbon nanoparticle exposure synergistically induce ASD-like phenotypes
PAPERS.pm: Carbon black nanoparticles, intranasal 95 ug/kg on gestational days 5 and 9
PAPERS.n: Pregnant C57BL/6N dams received intranasal carbon black nanoparticles (95 ug/kg) or water on GD5 and GD9; offspring were genotyped wild-type or Setd5+/- and analysed by sex. Only male Setd5+/- offspring exposed to CBNP showed a higher proportion with ASD-like behaviour (reduced social-novelty exploration, fixation on a familiar mouse) with selective loss of parvalbumin interneurons; either factor alone had minimal effect. Limitation: a single dose by intranasal bolus, a model particle without the metals or organics of ambient PM, and 'proportion of individuals' outcomes in small groups; group sizes are not in the abstract. Relevance: low-moderate - a gene-by-exposure synergy implies population risk is concentrated in susceptible genotypes that a mean exposure-response hides.

PAPERS.title: Metabolite-Associated Inflammation during Combined Exposure to Cooking Oil Fumes and Atopic Dermatitis: A Multi-Organ Spatial Metabolomics Study
PAPERS.pm: Cooking oil fume inhalation (controlled high-concentration regimen)
PAPERS.n: A mouse model of atopic dermatitis with cooking-oil-fume co-exposure, profiled by untargeted and spatial metabolomics with in situ immunofluorescence across lung, blood, heart and kidney. AD+COF gave the largest rises in IL-6 and TNF-a and the largest metabolite shifts: succinate accumulation, xanthine and uric-acid depletion, glucose perturbation and spatial lipid remodelling, correlated across organs. Limitation, stated by the authors: no tracing, receptor blockade or mitochondrial assays, so inter-organ signalling is associative, and the high-concentration regimen limits environmental extrapolation; COF particle size and mass are not given in the abstract. Relevance: low - indoor cooking PM is a large exposure class, but this design cannot inform a dose metric.

PAPERS.title: Integrated Assessment of Indoor Air Pollution and Associated Health Risks in a Hemodialysis Unit
PAPERS.pm: Indoor/outdoor PM0.3, PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO2; monthly VOC campaigns
PAPERS.n: One hemodialysis treatment room monitored for a year: ~1,400 time-resolved readings of CO2, O3 and PM0.3/2.5/10 with simultaneous outdoor measurements, plus 12 monthly VOC campaigns. Indoor CO2 often exceeded the Spanish threshold (indoor-outdoor difference >350 ppm, peaks >1,100 ppm), indicating poor ventilation. PM2.5, PM10 and O3 had I/O ratios below 1 (predominantly outdoor origin) and were generally under WHO guidelines with occasional peaks; most VOCs had I/O >1, and benzene and ethylbenzene cancer risks were below 1e-6. Limitation: one room, instrument type and PM calibration are not given in the abstract, and 'occasional peaks' are not quantified. Relevance: moderate - dialysis patients spend ~12 h/week indoors in one room; I/O ratios tell a facility whether filtration or ventilation is the lever.

PAPERS.title: Evaluating Indoor Air Pollution in Urban, Low-Income, Multi-Family Buildings: A Case Study from Indianapolis
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - indoor air pollution in low-income housing (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 1 Oct with no abstract; PubMed efetch, Europe PMC and Semantic Scholar returned nothing and Scholar Gateway is still disconnected. The title describes an indoor air-pollution evaluation in low-income multi-family buildings in an Indianapolis case study. Directly relevant to low-cost indoor sensor deployments in under-monitored housing. Nothing about data, method, sample size or estimates can be stated from the deposit, and this watch does not infer a method from a title. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Epigenetic Exposure Signatures Distinguish Early-Onset from Later-Onset Colorectal Cancer in a Racially Diverse US Cohort
PAPERS.pm: Methylation risk score for coarse PM (tumour tissue), not measured exposure
PAPERS.n: Applies published methylation risk scores (lifestyle, air pollution, pesticides) to tumour tissue from 146 DANCE colorectal-cancer cases (29 early-onset, 69 intermediate, 48 late) and relates them to age at onset, adjusting for race, geography, Area Deprivation Index and a multi-exposure index. Higher odds of early onset were associated with MRS for 2,4-D, heptachlor, coarse PM, Mediterranean diet and smoking. Limitation: decisive - MRS were trained on blood, applied here to tumour DNA, whose methylome is reshaped by the cancer itself; 29 early-onset cases; signatures are proxies validated against observed exposure only by Spearman correlation; no effect sizes in the abstract; preprint. Relevance: low - a coarse-PM methylation proxy is not an exposure measurement.
